headline: Wilderness Entry Permit Mandatory
reservation: A permit is required year-round. From May 1 through September 30, overnight trips and motorized day trips require quota permits; non-motorized day visits use self-issued permits. Outside that season, overnight visits also use self-issued permits. Confirm requirements for your entry point and travel mode.

days.title: Wilderness Orientation

stops.name: International Wolf Center
stops.detail: Learn about local ecology and the role of apex predators in the northern forest.

stops.name: Kawishiwi Falls Trail
stops.detail: A short, land-based hike to view the falls and acclimate to the local terrain.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local Ely transit; forest roads vary by weather.
days.note: Ensure all gear is organized and permits are in hand before heading to the launch.

days.title: Paddle and Portage Entry

stops.name: Designated Lake Campsite
stops.detail: Paddle to your permitted area and secure a site early as they are first-come, first-served.

stops.name: Lakeshore Exploring
stops.detail: Observe the shoreline for loons and bald eagles from the seat of your canoe.

days.driving: Canoe travel only; allow ample time for loading and portaging gear over land.
days.note: Wind can change rapidly; avoid large open-water crossings if whitecaps appear.

days.title: Base Camp and Interior Lakes

stops.name: Interior Portage Trail
stops.detail: Take a day trip to a neighboring lake to experience different scenery without moving camp.

stops.name: Shoreline Fishing Spot
stops.detail: Spend time on the water following local regulations for a quiet afternoon.

days.driving: Canoe travel only; distance depends on group stamina and wind conditions.
days.note: Always carry navigation tools and rain gear even on short day-trips from camp.

days.title: Wilderness Exit and Gateway

stops.name: Grand Marais Harbor
stops.detail: If using an eastern exit, explore the coastal shops and Lake Superior views.

stops.name: Gunflint Trail
stops.detail: Drive this scenic route to view interior forests from a paved roadway.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours for the drive from Ely to Grand Marais; conditions vary.
days.note: Confirm all rental gear is returned and checked according to your outfitter's schedule.

intel.title: Entry Point Lots
intel.text: Parking at wilderness entry points is limited and often involves narrow forest roads. Ensure your vehicle is within designated spaces to avoid blocking emergency access.

intel.title: Total Disconnect
intel.text: Expect zero cellular service once you enter the wilderness boundaries. Satellite messengers are suggested for emergency use, but do not rely on them for routine navigation.

intel.title: Gateway Fuel Stations
intel.text: Ely and Grand Marais are the final reliable fuel stops before heading into the forest. Top off your tank before driving to remote entry points like the Gunflint Trail.

intel.title: Daylight Constraints
intel.text: Setting up camp in the dark is hazardous in the wilderness. Plan to be off the water and have your shelter established at least two hours before sunset.

intel.title: Ice and Mud Season
intel.text: Spring access is highly dependent on ice-out dates which vary annually. Check the official Superior National Forest alerts before planning an early May trip.

plan.arrival: Fly into HIB and allow nearly 2.5 hours to reach Ely. Use the first afternoon to meet your outfitter, finalize gear, and verify permit pickup location.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance vehicle is recommended for unpaved forest access roads; check rental contracts for gravel road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: A calm lake shoreline offers the best vantage for evening light, though clarity depends on seasonal forest fire smoke or humidity.
